svg.title: Four Buckets Protect the Inventory Cycle
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Four Buckets Protect the Inventory Cycle; subtitle: Illustrative $200,000 startup stack, with $75,000 and $400,000 comparison allocations.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values are USD in the central $200,000 startup allocation. Each bucket uses the same percentage at the $75,000 lower and $400,000 upper endpoints, allowing proportional stacked comparison. Capital allocations are funding uses, not annual expense or revenue. The central allocation is not an additional earnings scenario.; caption: All three capital stacks reconcile: $75,000, $200,000, and $400,000. Protect cash for slow sales and repair surprises; an initial inventory purchase is not immediate recognized profit.; stages: label: Equipment acquisition reserve; value: $100,000 central allocation | 50% of capital; numeric value: 100000.0; detail: Lower stack: $37,500; central stack: $100,000; upper stack: $200,000. Fund serial-defined inventory within per-model exposure limits and documented buyer demand. Keep unsold equipment on the inventory ledger and review aging weekly.; label: Refurbishment and testing capacity; value: $40,000 central allocation | 20% of capital; numeric value: 40000.0; detail: Lower stack: $15,000; central stack: $40,000; upper stack: $80,000. Fund inspection, parts, bench work, calibrated test equipment access, decontamination, and service documentation. Separate durable tooling from unit-level inventory costs.; label: Operating cash buffer; value: $50,000 central allocation | 25% of capital; numeric value: 50000.0; detail: Lower stack: $18,750; central stack: $50,000; upper stack: $100,000. At the modeled $11,958 monthly Base-Case overhead, the central buffer covers about 4.2 months before direct inventory spending; a nine-month first-sale delay requires lower burn or additional funded liquidity.; label: Setup and transaction reserve; value: $10,000 central allocation | 5% of capital; numeric value: 10000.0; detail: Lower stack: $3,750; central stack: $10,000; upper stack: $20,000. Fund insurance deposits, inventory-system setup, initial packing materials, and specialist classification review. Track refundable deposits separately from expenses and avoid duplicating operating-buffer charges.

text.title: Four Buckets Protect the Inventory Cycle
text.tspan: Four Buckets Protect the Inventory Cycle

rect.title: label: Equipment acquisition reserve; numeric value: 100000.0; value: $100,000 central allocation | 50% of capital; detail: Lower stack: $37,500; central stack: $100,000; upper stack: $200,000. Fund serial-defined inventory within per-model exposure limits and documented buyer demand. Keep unsold equipment on the inventory ledger and review aging weekly.

text.title: Equipment acquisition reserve: $100,000 central allocation | 50% of capital
text.tspan: Equipment acquisition reserve: $100,000 central allocation | 50% of capital

rect.title: label: Refurbishment and testing capacity; numeric value: 40000.0; value: $40,000 central allocation | 20% of capital; detail: Lower stack: $15,000; central stack: $40,000; upper stack: $80,000. Fund inspection, parts, bench work, calibrated test equipment access, decontamination, and service documentation. Separate durable tooling from unit-level inventory costs.

text.title: Refurbishment and testing capacity: $40,000 central allocation | 20% of capital
text.tspan: Refurbishment and testing capacity: $40,000 central allocation | 20% of capital

rect.title: label: Operating cash buffer; numeric value: 50000.0; value: $50,000 central allocation | 25% of capital; detail: Lower stack: $18,750; central stack: $50,000; upper stack: $100,000. At the modeled $11,958 monthly Base-Case overhead, the central buffer covers about 4.2 months before direct inventory spending; a nine-month first-sale delay requires lower burn or additional funded liquidity.

text.tspan: Operating cash buffer: $50,000 central allocation | 25% of capital

rect.title: label: Setup and transaction reserve; numeric value: 10000.0; value: $10,000 central allocation | 5% of capital; detail: Lower stack: $3,750; central stack: $10,000; upper stack: $20,000. Fund insurance deposits, inventory-system setup, initial packing materials, and specialist classification review. Track refundable deposits separately from expenses and avoid duplicating operating-buffer charges.
